answers.answer: Rule is determined by warriors plus buildings. You rule a clearing if you have more total warriors and buildings there than every other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules; Eyrie win a tie for most if they have at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule and cannot prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: “more total warriors plus buildings”; “Tokens and pawns do not contribute”; “Eyrie rule a tie”; “Vagabond cannot rule”

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of your warriors or pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin or destination or both, and recheck rule for each move. You may move the same pieces repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answers.evidence: Move (4.2): positive number; rule origin or destination or both; same pieces repeatedly; rivers are not paths.

answers.answer: Battle is initiated in a clearing where you have warriors or a pawn and an enemy is present; you need not rule it. The defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits; otherwise it deals two immediate hits regardless of defending warriors, then is discarded. If no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends. Resolve before-roll effects, then roll: higher die is attacker's hits and lower is defender's (equal dice give equal results); each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Resolve after-roll effects; add extra hits and subtract ignored hits, with extra hits uncapped. If defender has no warriors, attacker deals one defenseless extra hit (Vagabond instead checks for undamaged swords). Each hit removes one opposing piece; the side taking hits chooses its own removal order, but warriors must be removed before buildings/tokens. Effects triggered by own piece removals are ordered by the affected side. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, even when defending or outside battle.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3): six steps from Ambush to Deal hits; “all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens”; whoever removes enemy building/token scores one VP each.

answers.answer: Crafting cost is the card's crafting icons at bottom left: activate one matching crafting piece per icon, not by paying the card's suit. A crafting piece normally activates only once per turn. Vagabond may reactivate its pawn for each icon by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer per icon. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from the map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Craft (4.1): icons completely define cost; each crafting piece once per turn except Vagabond hammer payments; item card requires item in supply; cannot craft identical persistent effect already in play.

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from your hand by putting it in your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. You win at the start of your own Birdsong if you rule three clearings of the matching mouse, rabbit, or fox suit, or, for bird dominance, two diagonally opposite corner clearings. The activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Dominance: “In own Daylight at at least 10 VP”; win condition at “start of own Birdsong”; “Cannot remove/replace activated card.”

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card may pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it and neither taking nor activation uses a faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Dominance: discard destination is near map; take available card during own Daylight by spending matching card; available bird dominance “remains bird”; taking and activation are separate.

answers.answer: With two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is two boots, two bags, one crossbow, one hammer, two swords, two tea and two coins. Only if Vagabond is in the game, hide its four R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword one beneath each ruin, shuffling the stacks so identities stay hidden; without Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Set up factions in order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This setup order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 and 7: two-player dominance removal, three-card draws, ruin and map item supply, Vagabond-only ruin items, faction letter order.

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed. Whenever Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply. This can happen outside battle. Without a Keep, Field Hospitals have no destination.
answers.evidence: Keep: only Marquise may place; cannot be placed again if removed. Field Hospitals: spend a matching card to put removed warriors in Keep clearing.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight begins by crafting with workshops, then allows up to three actions plus one for each bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number except Recruit's limit. March is one action of up to two moves and cannot be interrupted between moves to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise Daylight: craft first; up to three actions plus birds; March up to two moves as compound action; Recruit once; Overwork matching card.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and choose the building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the uncovered track space. Full wood cost, available building and a legal slot are required.
answers.evidence: Marquise Build procedure specifies rule, open slot, leftmost building, linked ruled-clearing wood payment, VP on uncovered space, and prerequisites.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, first draw one card if the Eyrie hand is empty (Emergency Orders). Then add one or two hand cards to the Decree, with at most one added bird card; each may go in any column. If there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Birdsong steps: Emergency Orders, Add to Decree, A New Roost; new roost clearing must allow placement of all pieces.

answers.answer: In Daylight, craft first using roosts, then resolve every Decree card by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column, card order is free and bird is wild. Recruit places one warrior at one chosen roost in a matching clearing (two with Charismatic). Move at least one warrior from a matching clearing under normal movement rules. Battle in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build a roost in a matching clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil begins immediately; you cannot skip it or continue other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Daylight Decree resolution: craft first; column order; each action requirements; any incomplete action causes immediate Turmoil.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP for every bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard all Decree cards except the Viziers. Flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement; if none are face up, flip them all face up first. Retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. End Daylight and proceed through the normal Evening: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, then discard to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
answers.evidence: Turmoil section lists VP loss including Viziers, card discard, leader replacement, retucking, full normal Evening and map pieces remaining.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card to Supporters (birds count); moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If no matching card including birds is available, the player shows their hand to Alliance and Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If the Supporters stack is full, discard the incoming card, but the payment or no-match draw still occurs.
answers.evidence: Outrage: triggers and card payment; no-match hand reveal and draw; full-stack incoming card discarded though payment/draw still occurs.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, complete all Revolts before beginning any Spread Sympathy; each action may be done any number of times, but cannot return to Revolt after spreading starts. For each action, supporters spent must match the target clearing; birds are wild. Revolt requires a sympathetic clearing with no base that matches a base still on the Alliance board; spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces, score one VP for each enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, place warriors equal to sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit (including this one), and one warrior in Officers. Enemy Vagabond instead damages three items. Spread Sympathy selects an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; pay the cost shown above the next token, plus one matching supporter if the selected clearing has at least three warriors of one other player (Martial Law). Place sympathy and score the uncovered VP; only one sympathy per clearing and Keep placement ban still applies.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong: all Revolts precede Spread Sympathy; supporters match target; procedures, eligibility, costs, Martial Law and outcomes listed.

answers.answer: In Daylight, Train by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, officers enable operations, including Organize: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there and score its uncovered VP. Organize is an Evening operation and spends no supporters. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Train and Organize rules; Losing a base: matching supporters, half officers rounded up, five supporter cap if no bases.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, Refresh flips two exhausted items face up per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed in this step adds no refresh. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects preventing movement out. Vagabond Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if possible. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening rules specify Refresh, Slip, boot costs, movement restrictions, Rest, and always drawing.

answers.answer: Explore: exhaust a torch in the ruin's clearing, take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, and score one VP if an item was taken; the ruin is removed and its slot freed when its last item is taken. Quest: in a matching clearing choose a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, complete it, and choose VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair: exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel, keeping its current face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight procedures for Explore, Quest and Repair list costs, eligibility and outcomes.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile, except the separate Allied-warrior battle-loss rule. During battle on your own turn, score one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made the faction Hostile. Thus hostile buildings/tokens normally yield two VP total each (one removal VP plus one Infamy), while a hostile warrior yields one Infamy unless it caused Hostility. Infamy depends on whose turn it is, not which side attacks; none is scored on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike targets one enemy warrior; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it target another faction piece.
answers.evidence: Hostile and Infamy rules; Aid cannot move Hostile marker; Strike target rule.

answers.answer: With four or more players, during own Daylight at 10 or more VP, Vagabond may activate dominance to coalition with another player not already in a coalition. The partner must have the lowest VP among players other than Vagabond; choose among ties. Place Vagabond's score marker on that faction board and stop scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition itself does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition paragraph states player-count, timing, VP, partner selection, victory and Hostile/Allied effects.

answers.answer: A card overrides the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. Use general and faction rules together where possible, and the faction rule prevails if incompatible. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden, so an ordinary card does not override it by implication.
answers.evidence: Precedence: “Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play”; faction rule wins incompatibility; “Cannot is absolute unless explicitly overridden.”

answers.answer: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. For battle effects at the same timing, the attacker chooses their order. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action, so you cannot interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player chooses unclear simultaneous effects; attacker orders same-timing battle effects; March's two moves are one compound action.

answers.answer: At-start effects occur before all other effects in that phase; at-end effects follow all other effects in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure defines “At start” and “at end” timing and prohibits other actions once last turn step begins.

answers.answer: Hand size is public but hand contents are private; reveal or show cards only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be inspected, but the deck cannot be inspected. Deals are non-binding; cards can be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules—Cards and information: hand size public, contents private; face-up piles inspectable, deck cannot; agreements non-binding, card transfers only as instructed, no consent needed for actions.

answers.answer: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Bird cards substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple cards of the same suit. When instructed to give or discard non-bird cards, birds must be treated as that suit; an explicit bird requirement cannot be paid with a non-bird.
answers.evidence: Cards: empty deck triggers immediate discard reshuffle; birds substitute for non-bird suits; forced non-bird give/discard uses birds; explicit bird requires bird.

answers.answer: Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. When instructed to place more pieces than can be placed, place the maximum possible and do not voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites and does not waive Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answers.evidence: Piece limit: “must do the maximum possible and cannot voluntarily do fewer”; never waives costs/prerequisites or Eyrie Decree obligations; “no proxies.”

answers.answer: Pieces placed normally come from supply or, for tracked pieces, the leftmost track space. Removed faction pieces normally return to supply or, for tracked pieces, the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answers.evidence: Removed pieces return to supply/rightmost track; placement from supply/leftmost track; items permanently removed; simultaneous pieces removed before effects trigger.

answers.answer: A forced action is resolved as if the affected player chose it, so that player's abilities and restrictions apply. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.
answers.evidence: Force: “Resolve forced actions as if affected player chose them, retaining their abilities and restrictions”; forced player makes battle decisions.

answers.answer: An enemy cannot replace a piece in the Keep clearing to bypass the Keep's placement ban: replacement requires both removal and legal placement to be possible. A swap ignores move and place restrictions, unlike a move or placement.
answers.evidence: Replace requires removal and placement possible; Keep placement ban cannot be bypassed; Swap ignores move/place restrictions.

answers.answer: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.
answers.evidence: 30 VP: simultaneous tie goes to player closest clockwise to current player, including current player.

answers.answer: A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path and to forests separated from it by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests. Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest using those forest adjacency rules. Fall has no special rules.
answers.evidence: Forest definition includes clearing/forest adjacency and Winter river; Overview says Fall has no special rules.

answers.answer: Marquise starts with 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner; put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings, in any combination that respects slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.
answers.evidence: Marquise setup (6.3) gives supplies, corner and warrior placements, initial buildings, and track arrangement.

answers.answer: Eyrie supplies 20 warriors. Place one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep the others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Fill the roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.
answers.evidence: Eyrie setup (7.3) states warrior supply, corner placement, leader and Viziers, and remaining roost track.

answers.answer: Alliance supplies 10 warriors; place its three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. It starts with no map pieces and no officers.
answers.evidence: Alliance setup (8.3): ten warriors, three bases, ten sympathy, three additional Supporters cards, no map pieces/officers.

answers.answer: Choose Thief, Tinker or Ranger and place the Vagabond pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's listed S-marked starting items: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks, and other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. Put each other faction's relationship marker at Indifferent.
answers.evidence: Vagabond setup (9.3) specifies pawn, quests, starting item placement and relationships.

answers.answer: Recommended Reach totals are at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5 and Alliance 3. The Law permits adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.
answers.evidence: Recommended faction mix (5.2): Reach thresholds and faction values; any mix totaling at least 17 allowed.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, Marquise places one wood per sawmill in that sawmill's clearing (one per sawmill even if multiple share a clearing), limited by the finite supply of eight wood. During Daylight, Overwork can also place one wood by spending a card matching a sawmill clearing. In Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answers.evidence: Wood production and Marquise Birdsong describe one wood per sawmill and eight-wood limit; Evening draw rule.

answers.answer: Recruit is once per turn and places one warrior at each recruiter. If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place the maximum available and choose among eligible recruiters where to place them.
answers.evidence: Marquise Recruit: one at each recruiter, once per turn; if supply short, maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters.

answers.answer: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of their printed VP under Disdain for Trade. Builder ignores Disdain and therefore scores the printed item VP. Other extra crafting-point effects still apply under Disdain.
answers.evidence: Eyrie special rules: items score one VP instead of printed; Builder ignores Disdain; other extra crafting-point effects still apply.

answers.answer: Builder: Viziers in Recruit and Move; ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic: Recruit and Battle; each Recruit must place two warriors. Commander: Move and Battle; one extra hit as attacker. Despot: Move and Build; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP beyond normal removal points.
answers.evidence: Eyrie leader table gives each Vizier column and ability.

answers.answer: No. With Charismatic, each Recruit must place two warriors. If only one remains, the Recruit action cannot be fully completed and the Eyrie enters Turmoil; the general maximum-placement rule does not waive the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answers.evidence: Charismatic Recruit must place two; incomplete Decree action causes Turmoil; piece shortage does not waive Eyrie Decree obligation.

answers.answer: No. Guerrilla War changes which die the Alliance uses when defending, but warrior caps still apply. Alliance uses the higher die and the attacker uses the lower die.
answers.evidence: Guerrilla War: Alliance defending reverses dice; warrior caps still apply.

answers.answer: No. Supporters may be spent only for suit, so they cannot be used to craft; they are inspectable by Alliance. They are separate from hand cards and do not count toward the five-card hand limit.
answers.evidence: Supporters are inspectable by Alliance, usable only for suit, and do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit.

answers.answer: No. All Revolts must be completed before Spread Sympathy begins. Once spreading starts, the Alliance cannot return to Revolt during that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot support a same-Birdsong Revolt.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong: all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy; cannot return to Revolt; newly spread sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong Revolt.

answers.answer: No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors of one other player, not two warriors each from two different players. The extra matching supporter is a Spread Sympathy cost; it does not increase Organize's cost.
answers.evidence: Martial Law applies with three warriors of one other player; Organize explicitly has no Martial Law cost.

answers.answer: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage, and moving only the Vagabond pawn there does not either. If allied warriors accompany the Vagabond and are moved into sympathy, their movement triggers Outrage.
answers.evidence: Outrage: placing warriors and moving only Vagabond pawn do not trigger; moving Allied warriors into sympathy triggers Outrage.

answers.answer: In Evening, the Alliance may take military operations up to its number of officers, in any order and repetition. Using an operation does not consume an officer. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Evening operations up to officers; officers stay and are not consumed; draw after operations.

answers.answer: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. If an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, the pawn is instead left there and three Vagabond items are damaged.
answers.evidence: Pawn and items: pawn “cannot be removed”; all-enemy-pieces effect instead damages three items.

answers.answer: Vagabond's rolled-hit maximum, whether attacking or defending, equals all undamaged swords in Satchel, face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. As defender it is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Excess hits damage one undamaged item per hit; once no undamaged items remain, excess hits are ignored.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Battle: maximum hits use all undamaged swords face up or down; defenseless only with none; excess hits ignored when no undamaged items remain.

answers.answer: Face-up tea, coins and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting a tracked item sends it to Satchel. Damaged items cannot pay for actions, even if face up; action costs require a face-up, undamaged item.
answers.evidence: Pawn and items: tea/coins/bags move from Satchel to tracks; three-item track cap; exhausting track item returns it to Satchel; damaged items cannot pay.

answers.answer: Capacity is six items plus two for each face-up bag on its track. Count items in Satchel plus Damaged box; track items do not count. Check capacity at the end of Evening after discard, permanently removing chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit. Do not check immediately when acquiring an item.
answers.evidence: Evening capacity rule specifies six plus two per face-up track bag, included/excluded areas, timing and permanent removal.

answers.answer: No. Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh occurs in Birdsong and flips exhausted items; Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel while keeping its current face.
answers.evidence: Evening Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items; Birdsong Refresh; Repair preserves current face.

answers.answer: Aid exhausts any one item and gives a card matching the Vagabond's clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. A crafted item is not required; the Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items box if available. To advance a non-Hostile relationship, Aid the faction the number of times printed between the current and next spaces during the same turn; each Aid counts for one improvement. Further Aid to an Allied faction scores two VP each.
answers.evidence: Aid procedure and Relationships section: any item, matching card, faction pieces in clearing, optional item; repeated same-turn Aid thresholds and Allied scoring.

answers.answer: At Allied status, each subsequent Aid to that faction scores two VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany a move to the destination; they follow their own movement restrictions and cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. At the start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may treat warriors of one Allied faction there as its own, but cannot use that faction's warriors to attack the ally itself.
answers.evidence: Allied benefits table specifies Aid points, accompanying movement restrictions, and attacking with one ally's warriors and exception.

answers.answer: In a battle where Vagabond uses Allied warriors as its own, it may absorb hits by removing those warriors or damaging items. At battle end, the ally becomes Hostile if Vagabond removed more allied warriors than items it damaged in that battle. Equal numbers do not cause Hostility.
answers.evidence: Taking hits with an ally: compare removed allied warriors with items damaged; Hostile at battle end only if warriors removed exceed items damaged.

answers.answer: No. The pawn supplies a crafting piece matching its current clearing, so that clearing must match all crafting icons; one clearing cannot meet mixed fox and rabbit requirements. Vagabond may reactivate its pawn for multiple icons by exhausting one face-up, undamaged hammer per icon. A crafted item can immediately be taken face up into Satchel or its track.
answers.evidence: Craft: pawn suit is current clearing; must match all icons and cannot craft mixed suits from one clearing; each icon requires hammer; item can be taken immediately.

answers.answer: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea and sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag and hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow and sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items while keeping their faces, immediately ending Daylight and beginning Evening.
answers.evidence: Base character table lists starting items, special actions, costs/results, and Ranger timing.

answers.answer: When Explore takes the last item from a ruin, remove the ruin and free its building slot. Ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin; ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed.
answers.evidence: Explore removes ruin when last item taken; general clearing rules say ruins block slots and can be removed only when explicitly allowed.

answers.answer: No. Coalition partners are not enemies. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition: “Coalition partners are not enemies”; coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers.

answers.answer: The total is 5 VP. Removing two warriors and one building yields 3 removal VP. The first warrior that makes the faction Hostile is exempt from Infamy; the second hostile warrior gives 1 Infamy VP, and the subsequently removed hostile building gives 1 Infamy in addition to its 1 removal VP. Infamy applies because this is Vagabond's turn and it is battle.
answers.evidence: Each removed building/token gives one VP; hostile pieces removed in battle on own turn add one Infamy each, except the warrior that first caused Hostility.

answers.answer: A destination with hostile buildings but no hostile warriors requires only the normal one boot. A destination with hostile warriors from one or several Hostile factions requires one extra boot total, in addition to the normal boot; the rule says any warriors of any Hostile faction, not one extra per faction.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Move: one boot plus one extra if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; Hostile status requires extra boot for warriors, not merely buildings/tokens.

answers.answer: No. Taking an available dominance card puts it in hand; activating it is a separate choice. Taking and activating dominance cards do not require a faction action allowance, so neither uses a Marquise action.
answers.evidence: Dominance: taking available card and activation are separate; neither requires a faction action allowance.

answers.answer: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: each player owns their chosen faction and its listed pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.
answers.evidence: Components: “Faction-piece ownership cannot change”; items are not faction pieces and possession does not confer faction ownership.

answers.answer: An immediate-effect card is resolved and discarded; an item card also requires the item in map supply, then the item goes to Crafted Items and listed VP is scored (subject to Eyrie's exception). A persistent-effect card stays in the play area and grants its text. A card there is outside your hand and cannot be spent, discarded or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
answers.evidence: Craft: immediate effects resolve/discard; persistent effects stay in play and cannot be spent/discarded/used unless explicitly instructed.

answers.answer: Ambush cards cannot be crafted; the defender may play one for two immediate hits, or the attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. Dominance cards cannot be crafted; activate one to change the victory condition or spend it for suit.
answers.evidence: Craft section: Ambush and Dominance cannot be crafted; lists their permitted uses.

answers.answer: Choose factions, then determine starting player and seating randomly. Put score markers at zero and set aside the battle dice nearby. Factions set up in letter order—Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond—but setup order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Standard Setup steps 1–2 and 6–7: random starter/seating, score markers zero, dice nearby, faction setup order distinct from turn order.

answers.answer: The first player to reach 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; they need not finish the action, phase or turn.
answers.evidence: 30 VP: first to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn.

answers.answer: To initiate battle, choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy there as defender. Battle does not require you to rule the clearing.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3): choose a clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy as defender; no rule requirement.

answers.answer: At the same timing, the attacker chooses the order of applicable before-roll effects if both players have them, and likewise for after-roll effects. The side whose pieces are removed chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its pieces.
answers.evidence: Battle: attacker chooses order of before/after-roll effects; side taking hits chooses order of effects triggered by its own pieces' removal.

answers.answer: In Count Hits, add extra hits, then subtract ignored hits. Extra hits are uncapped by warriors.
answers.evidence: Battle Count Hits: add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits.

answers.answer: A non-Vagabond faction crafting an item card takes the item from the map supply into its Crafted Items box and scores the card's listed VP, with the Eyrie's Disdain exception. Ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as the Vagabond does.
answers.evidence: Craft immediate effect: item must be in supply; take it into Crafted Items and score listed VP subject to Eyrie exception; ordinary factions do not exhaust items.

answers.answer: Eyrie activate roosts and Alliance activate sympathy. The crafting piece's suit is the suit of its clearing. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.
answers.evidence: Craft: Marquise workshops, Eyrie roosts, Alliance sympathy; piece suit is its clearing suit; three-color question mark accepts any suit.

answers.answer: Mobilize adds a hand card to Supporters, respecting the supporter capacity. During Daylight, Alliance may Craft, Mobilize and Train in any order and any number, so it need not finish crafting before Mobilizing or Training.
answers.evidence: Alliance Daylight: any order and number; Mobilize adds hand card to Supporters, respecting cap.

answers.answer: In Evening, Eyrie scores the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draws one card plus uncovered draw bonuses and discards down to five. This full normal Evening still happens after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Evening scoring/draw/discard; Turmoil proceeds to the full normal Evening.

answers.answer: Vagabond exhausts one sword to initiate its Battle action. The sword must be ready and undamaged to pay the cost. An exhausted sword cannot pay, even though an undamaged exhausted sword still counts toward rolled-hit maximum.
answers.evidence: Battle action exhausts one sword; actions require face-up undamaged items; rolled-hit maximum counts undamaged swords face up or down.

answers.answer: Each turn proceeds Birdsong, Daylight, Evening. Players take turns clockwise, so after a player's Evening the next player clockwise begins their Birdsong.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: turns clockwise; Birdsong → Daylight → Evening.

answers.answer: A hit damages one undamaged item chosen by Vagabond and sends it to the Damaged box without changing its face. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit; excess hits are ignored when there are no undamaged items remaining.
answers.evidence: Damaging an item sends it to Damaged box without changing face; one hit damages an undamaged item; ignore excess when none remain.

answers.answer: Alliance may take up to its number of officers' military operations in Evening. For one Recruit operation, place one warrior at one clearing with a base.
answers.evidence: Alliance operations table: operations up to officers; Recruit places one warrior at one clearing with a base.

answers.answer: The Vagabond can take any number of Daylight actions in any order, as ready undamaged items permit. The action types do not have a fixed order, and the same type may be repeated.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Daylight: any order/number as ready undamaged items permit.

answers.answer: Strike requires exhausting one crossbow. It must be face up and undamaged to pay the cost; an exhausted or damaged crossbow cannot pay.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Strike: exhaust crossbow; general item rule says action cost requires a face-up, undamaged item.
